verdict_reason: The goals are sound, but the routing, diversity, availability and requirement contracts need precise semantics before implementation.
reply_markdown:
## Framing
The brief assumes usefulness ratings, lab labels and panel size are adequate proxies for review value. Missing alternatives: deterministic stratified rotation; Thompson/UCB routing; scoring verified-finding precision instead of judge satisfaction; diversity based on observed correlated errors or endpoint groups; operator-pinned members plus automatic fill; and budget-aware selection using cost, latency and quota. I would choose only after knowing rating volume/sparsity, its correlation with structured replies, panel budgets, cost/latency distributions, correlated failures by lab/endpoint, and whether the objective is defect discovery, independent consensus or reliable acceptance.

## Q1
Use a confidence-weighted rate, not the additive sum. For example `(yes + 0.5*partly + 2)/(rated + 4)` or a Beta posterior lower bound, hierarchically shrunk from all-purpose to purpose/topic evidence. The proposed sum rewards exposure without normalizing and its floor collapses all negative histories. Keep recency decay rather than a hard 90-day cliff.

## Q2
Exploration 0.2 per slot is plausible only cold: for four slots it expects 0.8 explorations and gives about 60% of panels at least one. It becomes expensive once evidence accumulates. Decay it with effective sample size or use posterior sampling; cap exploratory slots at one per panel.

## Q3
Yes. If lab A has scores 10 and 9.5 while lab B has 0.25, size 2 selects 10 and 0.25 instead of 10 and 9.5. Make diversity a soft bonus or reserve one seat only when candidates' confidence intervals overlap or scores are within a documented tolerance.

## Q4
Keep roles prompt-only. `codex-consult.ps1:713-735,936-939` already gives purpose presets and explicit overrides; silently changing effort or words by role would confound comparisons and telemetry. Permit explicit `-Effort`/`-MaxWords` as today.

## Q5
Judge quota/auth outages at the shared endpoint-group level, then project the state onto every affected roster entry. Display compact groups such as `gemini :: m1,m2 (until ...)` rather than provider-only rows or ambiguous `*`; show `all N reviewers available` otherwise. This preserves one line without losing actionable identity.

## Verified / inferred
Verified: roster validation and selection (`codex-consult-common.ps1:4589-5005`), rating persistence and joins (`codex-findings.ps1:395-427`; `codex-scoreboard.ps1:119-182`), presets and panel IDs (`codex-consult.ps1:713-745,1221-1237`), health (`codex-consult-common.ps1:4425-4507`), hook/provider output (`codex-consult-hook.ps1:62-92`; `codex-providers.ps1:245-329`), and existing tests. Statistical, operational and quota-sharing consequences are inferred; no new code or tests were run.

findings.claim: The additive score `1 + yes + 0.5*partly - no` with floor 0.25 is volume-sensitive and lets accumulated exposure dominate observed quality; the floor also maps every sufficiently bad history to the same value.
findings.trigger: One lineage has many slightly positive ratings while another has one clean positive rating, or two lineages have several negative ratings.

evidence.observation: ratings are only accumulated as yes/partly/no counters per lineage and purpose.
normalizing by sample size is absent, so score grows with rating count.

findings.verification: Construct synthetic histories with equal rates but different counts and compare the proposed score against a Beta-smoothed rate.
findings.remedy: Use a smoothed usefulness rate or posterior lower confidence bound, with hierarchical purpose/topic shrinkage and optional time decay.

findings.claim: Ratings and consultation numbers are task-scoped, so joining cross-task telemetry by `n` alone can attach a rating to the wrong consultation and therefore the wrong topics or lineage.
findings.trigger: Two task ledgers both contain consultation n=1 and routing aggregates every task as the design specifies.

evidence.observation: Read-AllTaskConsults flattens consultations from every task without a task key.
the existing scoreboard resets `keyOf` inside each task loop, proving n is unique only within a task.
-Rate resolves n within one task's sessions.json and copies lineage/purpose into the rating.

findings.verification: Create two temporary task ledgers with n=1 and different topics, rate one, then run a prototype aggregate and inspect attribution.
findings.remedy: Key evidence by `(task, n)` or consult_id everywhere; retain task identity in the aggregate input and validate rating.consult_id as well as n.

findings.claim: The 90-day window is undefined and re-rating can make old evidence look recent, while ratings are missing-not-at-random because the skill says structured responders are preferentially rated.
findings.trigger: An old consultation is re-rated, or a prose/failed reviewer receives fewer ratings than a structured reviewer, before automated routing consumes the data.

evidence.observation: re-rating replaces the record and the new mark carries the current timestamp.
the documentation explicitly warns that telemetry is biased toward reviewers answering JSON.

findings.verification: Re-rate a consultation older than 90 days and check whether a prototype score includes it based on `when` rather than consultation completion.
findings.remedy: Define recency by consultation completion; retain rating history and rate-time metadata, and model or report rating propensity before optimizing selection.

findings.claim: Topic scoring is underspecified: normalization, deduplication, missing-topic fallback, multi-topic credit and the mean-of-means can double-count one judgment or dilute strong purpose evidence.
findings.trigger: A consultation has topics `[security,tests]` and one rating, or a request has one topic with no ratings but purpose ratings exist.

evidence.observation: current aggregation has no topics dimension or topic join.
one rating counted for every consultation topic and then averaged with purpose scores reuses the same evidence multiple times.

findings.verification: Feed one multi-topic rating through candidate formulas and compare its influence with a single-topic rating.
findings.remedy: Specify canonical topic normalization, fractional multi-topic credit, and a hierarchical fallback; average weighted evidence rather than independent means.

findings.claim: Diversity-before-rank can deterministically displace a clearly superior second model of a large lab with a near-useless representative of a small lab.
findings.trigger: Labs A has scores 10 and 9.5 and lab B has 0.25; the requested size is two.

evidence.observation: current selection has only roster order and weighty eligibility; the proposed fill layer has no quality tolerance.
one representative per distinct lab is mandatory before rank fills remaining seats.

findings.verification: Run selection with the stated synthetic scores and assert whether the 9.5 candidate is excluded.
findings.remedy: Use soft diversity scoring, a quality-gap threshold, or one diversity reserve seat rather than a hard first pass.

findings.claim: Panel-size semantics leave `none`/`chore`, `-PanelSize` combined with `-PanelAll`, overlarge sizes, and ordering of availability/weighty/routing filters undefined; implementations can count skipped or merely planned members differently.
findings.trigger: `-Panel -Purpose chore -PanelSize 5`, or `-PanelAll -PanelSize 2`, with one unavailable and one weighty entry.

evidence.observation: Select-PanelMembers currently returns all entries with run/skipped state and no size parameter.
the panel run selects members before generating the panel identifier and does not define size precedence.

findings.verification: Dry-run the listed combinations against a fake roster and compare runner counts and reasons.
findings.remedy: Define defaults for every purpose including none/chore, make explicit size override the cap unless `-PanelAll` is explicit, and count only final State=run members after every filter.

findings.claim: Seeding with the panel id cannot reproduce a draw as specified because the id is generated after selection and afresh for every invocation, including dry runs; no user-supplied seed exists.
findings.trigger: Run the same dry run twice with identical inputs and expect the documented same-seed reproduction.

evidence.observation: selection occurs before `[guid]::NewGuid()` creates panelId.
the dry run reports a newly generated panel id rather than accepting a replay seed.

findings.verification: Invoke identical fake dry runs twice and compare printed routing picks for equal inputs.
findings.remedy: Generate or accept the routing seed before selection, record it, and define an exact portable PRNG and canonical candidate ordering; use the resulting panel id only as identity.

findings.claim: The no-ratings fallback and `-PanelOrder roster` contract contradict themselves: equal-weight draws shuffle, yet the text also says no ratings means roster order, and it does not say whether exploration and diversity still apply.
findings.trigger: A fresh repository has no ratings and runs a size-three panel twice.

evidence.observation: the brief explicitly poses and then rejects 'equal weights = roster order' while retaining both statements.
today's walk is explicitly roster order.

findings.verification: Specify and test a state table for `{no ratings, ratings} x {default, roster} x {diversity}` and compare expected orders.
findings.remedy: Make `-PanelOrder roster` a pure roster-order mode with size and eligibility only; when ratings are absent use that mode by default and record the fallback reason.

findings.claim: A quota failure without a known reset is represented inconsistently: health already gives it a 60-minute Until, roster walks skip it, but provider rows and the hook only change availability for QuotaKnown, so they still report the endpoint available.
findings.trigger: A 429 quota failure with no Retry-After occurs at 10:31 and SessionStart runs at 10:40.

evidence.observation: the record gets Until=when+60 minutes while QuotaKnown remains false.
verdicts become unavailable only when QuotaKnown is true.
the hook simply renders the provider verdict.

findings.verification: Seed a fake quota failure without retry_after and compare roster, provider, hook and explicit-run outcomes at +10 and +61 minutes.
findings.remedy: Make one shared availability verdict treat unknown-reset quota as out until `Until`, with the requested human wording, consistently across every surface and bypass rule.

findings.claim: The hook cannot show availability per roster entry because codex-providers emits one row per provider label and records only the first roster position/model; multi-model labels collapse or disappear.
findings.trigger: The roster has `gemini :: pro` and `gemini :: flash`, or two openai models, with one unavailable.

evidence.observation: rows are provider/engine-label rows and roster_position is the first matching entry.
the line renders row name plus verdict, not reviewer lineage.

findings.verification: Run `codex-providers.ps1 -Json -NoNetwork` with two models on one label and compare row count with roster entry count.
findings.remedy: Emit per-entry availability records while retaining endpoint/group fields, and format outages by lineage with compact grouping only when all affected models share the same state.

findings.claim: Endpoint-group availability is ill-defined because Get-PanelPlan computes groups only from selected runners, while an outage must propagate across every roster entry sharing credentials or quota even when that entry is not selected.
findings.trigger: Two agy labels share a Google quota but panel size one selects only a codex member, or required checks inspect an unselected agy entry.

evidence.observation: group construction receives Runners and merges labels only for those runners.
Q5 requires a group decision independent of the eventual panel pick.

findings.verification: Build a roster with shared-fingerprint labels and one different selected runner, then compare group membership for availability and concurrency.
findings.remedy: Define credential/quota groups over all resolved roster identities separately from scheduling groups; share outage state through that stable map.

findings.claim: `-Require` and roster `require` lack a complete contract and can silently proceed: required available members can lose their seats to size/diversity draws, matching and precedence are unspecified, and current fail-closed roster validation rejects the new keys.
findings.trigger: Acceptance requires openai, but PanelSize 2 selects two higher-ranked members; or a roster adds `lab`/`require` without another schema change.

evidence.observation: unknown top-level and entry keys make the roster unusable.
selection does not reserve or validate required identities.
the design defines unavailability refusal but not forced inclusion, engine suffix matching, CLI/default precedence, or interactions with -SkipPreflight/-Thread/no roster.

findings.verification: Dry-run cases where a required available reviewer falls below the panel cap and where CLI and roster requirements conflict; assert exit 5 and no writes.
findings.remedy: Pin required eligible members before filling seats; define canonical lineage matching including engine, wildcard policy, union/override precedence, all invocation modes, exit 5 and dry-run behavior; bump/extend roster validation.

findings.claim: Role loading is unsafe and ambiguous: name validation, traversal, plugin-versus-repository precedence, exact insertion point relative to the output contract/schema, and `-Role`/`-Roles` conflict or count mismatch are unspecified; assigning roles to randomized pick order also makes member-role pairing nondeterministic.
findings.trigger: A repository defines `.collab/roles/../../x.md`, shadows a built-in role, or passes more `-Roles` values than the panel size.

evidence.observation: prompt assembly is ordered and currently has no role insertion or source record.
the panel record currently has no role assignment map.

findings.verification: Dry-run traversal, shadowing, mismatched role counts and repeated members with a fixed routing seed and inspect exact prompt/ledger output.
findings.remedy: Restrict role names to a slug, resolve only declared directories with explicit precedence, forbid `-Role` with `-Roles`, define count rules, and assign roles by stable roster position or explicit lineage mapping rather than draw order.

findings.claim: The proposed fake-only test list omits high-risk boundaries: task-local n collisions, re-rating recency, rating bias/decay, topic fallback and multi-topic credit, lab normalization and quality gaps, size precedence, deterministic PRNG across PowerShell versions, unknown-reset transitions, shared endpoint outages, -Require pinning/precedence, role path safety and overflow behavior of the one-line hook.
findings.trigger: Acceptance relies on the listed happy-path tests after implementation.

evidence.observation: the test plan lists basic sizes, one diversity case, formula cuts, reproducibility/rate, records and roles.
existing health unit tests cover completion ordering but not the new shared-outage and unknown-reset display contract.
existing quota/provider tests establish the current inconsistent unknown-reset behavior but no new assertions exist.

findings.verification: Run the expanded deterministic harness matrix under both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 and require exact outputs, not statistical pass criteria.
findings.remedy: Add explicit cases for every boundary above; replace 'exploration at the recorded rate' flakiness with fixed-seed exact sequences plus a separately bounded statistical sanity check.

findings.claim: The documented claim that findings repeat past about five diverse members has no repository evidence or measurement definition and can become an unjustified selection cap.
findings.trigger: The README rule is used to size panels or stop adding reviewers.

evidence.observation: the telemetry section describes usefulness counts but no diminishing-returns study or repetition metric exists.
the brief proposes documenting the threshold but cites no dataset.

findings.verification: Measure marginal unique verified findings per added member over historical panels and report uncertainty before publishing a threshold.
findings.remedy: Label five as an operational heuristic and instrument marginal unique findings before making it a rule.

unproven: Actual rating volume and missingness by reviewer, purpose and reply format are unknown.
PowerShell 5.1 versus 7 RNG reproducibility was not executed.
Real provider quota sharing and reset-message parsing were inferred from code comments and tests, not live endpoints.
The claim that lab diversity improves independent defect discovery is not measured in this repository.
